relations.note: Xolotl is Quetzalcoatl’s canine manifestation, nahualli, alter ego, or divine counterpart.
Modern translations sometimes call Xolotl Quetzalcoatl’s twin, though literal shared birth is unattested.

relations.myth: Retrieval of ancestral bones from Mictlan
relations.note: Modern syntheses make Xolotl Quetzalcoatl’s companion, but the core Nahuatl passage is ambiguous.
relations.source: Leyenda de los Soles and later retellings

relations.myth: Sacrifice of the gods for the Fifth Sun
relations.note: Xolotl flees Ehecatl through successive transformations but is found and killed.
Nanahuatzin becomes the sun; Xolotl later resists the gods’ required deaths.
relations.source: Sahaguntine accounts; Leyenda de los Soles

relations.note: Tecuciztecatl becomes the moon before Xolotl resists the collective divine sacrifice.
The new sun remains motionless until the gods die; Xolotl evades that death.
Modern synthesis portrays Xolotl guiding the sun through the underworld each night.
Later astronomical reconstructions contrast evening-star Xolotl with the dawn or Morning-Star deity.

relations.myth: Retrieval of ancestral bones from Mictlan
relations.note: Later retellings place Xolotl beside Quetzalcoatl during the confrontation over ancestral bones.

relations.myth: Retrieval of ancestral bones from Mictlan
relations.note: Some modern retellings include her with Xolotl, without secure early attestation.
A colonial gloss links Chantico-Cuaxolotl with Xolotl’s headgear or insignia.
They appear within the same pictorial sequence, though no discrete encounter is certain.
Samael Aun Weor equates Xolotl with Lucifer in modern Gnostic sexual-alchemical doctrine.
Modern popular accounts equate the canine funerary deities without evidence of historical contact.
